result:
I made no changes this run. Seven FEBio pilot runs are healthy, one finished with an error, and both queues are empty.

- **Running:** 4 pilotCS runs (p061, p083, p129, p120) and 3 pilotCR9 runs (p061, p083, p129), at t = 2.70–3.35. Every log was updated in the last 6 s, each thread has its own core, so no re-pinning was needed.
- **Resources:**
  - CPU: 23.3 of 32 quota cores in use, no throttling.
  - Memory: 134.3 of 137.4 GB, but only 21.8 GB is real use; the rest is cache that can be freed. No out-of-memory kills.
  - GPUs: my runs are on GPUs 1–4, and GPUs 5 and 6 are idle for me. The 88 % reading on GPU 1 was a single snapshot; averaged over 10 s it is 40 %.
- **Failure:** pilotCR9_p120 ended with "failed to converge at time 2.76748" at 12:02. It is a solver problem, not a machine or scheduler one, so a restart would fail at the same point; I did not restart it. pilotCR9_p083 is now at t = 2.761, just before that point.
- **Idle:** about 9 cores and GPUs 5 and 6 have had nothing to do since 12:03, because neither queue has any waiting work. Someone needs to decide the next batch.
- **Services:** all are up. `resume_all.sh` starts the watchdog, which keeps the scheduler, GPU sampler and preflight running.
- **Still open:**
  - The split windows (`w_*`) of the 7 runs can't restart on their own after a scheduler restart or server stop.
  - The scheduler fills the lowest-numbered GPU first (up to 5 runs), so GPU 1 carries 3 runs while GPUs 5 and 6 sit empty. I measured no slowdown. Changing this means restarting the scheduler, which has to wait until no split run is running.

The report is `work/agents/foreman/report_20261104_1227.md`. I also overwrote `status.json` and added one line to `foreman_actions.log`.
